detail.description: Once upon a time, in the land of Really Not Far, there was a great election. As four candidates stand before the people, a new sovereign must be chosen. By electing their king or queen, the audience shapes the world that will unfold before their eyes. From that moment on, the story follows a path dictated by their choice: will their leader lead them to prosperity, or will they have unknowingly sealed a fate with darker consequences? Around a gigantic bouncy castle, this acrobatic tale invites the audience to take part in a playful yet powerful reminder of the importance of our voices and our actions. Make circus, not war!

The acrobatic lifts give height to the stories, making them as delirious and spectacular as they are sincere and touching. This quintet blends acrobatic lifts, theatrical acting and dark humor to tackle important themes in a world on the move. Through their unique universe, they offer a reflection that is admittedly wacky, but deeply rooted in today's concerns.

detail.description: A straw wall separates two gardens, where a girl grows up on one side and a boy on the other. Just like their idols Romeo and Juliet, their love is impossible because of the terrible hatred tearing their fathers apart. But in reality, the two fathers are great friends and pretend to hate each other so that their children, tempted by the forbidden, will fall in love and marry. The wall could then be torn down, their two lands joined into one and (above all) their taxes drastically reduced. As a final stratagem, they call on Straforel, a failed former actor now retrained as a “professional kidnapper” but... Suspense. After Molière's Le Mariage Forcé at Chalon dans la rue 2024, welcome to this little-known gem by Rostand, where popular comedy, interaction and music from the 2000s are once again in front of, behind, around and with the audience.

summary: Far from being content to “show,” the ADM company invites the audience to embark on a collective, acrobatic adventure. Through a truck journey, they explore life's challenges, where...

detail.description: Far from being content to “show,” the ADM company invites the audience to embark on a collective, acrobatic adventure. Through a truck journey, they explore life's challenges, where solitude becomes a strength and the group a landmark. The vehicle comes to life, unfolds and turns into a stage with the audience's help, creating fleeting but powerful bonds. This show breaks down the traditional barriers between artists and spectators. The audience becomes an actor, moving around, shifting perspective, and even taking part in transforming the set and in the acrobatics. Through spectacular acrobatics (hand to hand, Chinese pole), the artists weave a universe that is both technical and human, where the softness of interaction meets the stiffness of the machine. A vibrant moment of sharing, where every instant and every gesture creates a bond bigger than ourselves.

title: Main(s) Tenant(es)

detail.description: This show is above all an intimate exploration of the role of the base in acrobatics: a role that is often misunderstood, sometimes even erased, yet essential. In the discipline of hand to hand, the flyer who rises and spins draws every eye with their airborne movements. Yet behind every flyer stands a solid base, anchored to the ground, who guarantees safety, absorbs the weight and takes risks. This show seeks to reverse that usual dynamic to put the base and their relationship with their partner in the spotlight. In this solo, the partner and flyer is a landing mat. A seemingly simple and ordinary object, it deeply symbolizes the role of the base in the circus world. The mat becomes the analogy of the base artist: it absorbs falls, takes impacts and acts as a constant partner, each reflecting the other.

title: Les grandes eaux
tagline: Retro-futuristic distortion for a woman and a cargo trike
summary: Cécile Laloy tells the whimsical story of a metamorphosis in this choreographic piece written through paradoxes. It is not a story, it is a vertigo, a movement, a distortion. It...

detail.description: Cécile Laloy tells the whimsical story of a metamorphosis in this choreographic piece written through paradoxes. It is not a story, it is a vertigo, a movement, a distortion. It is the end of one world and the passage to another. A woman and her vehicle, both survivors of an era that has lost its bearings, navigate a space-time bubble. She borrows from the figure of the clown and fights several battles against her fear, her own transformation, her pregnancy, her molting. She crosses the great waters, and crosses herself like the I Ching, the Book of Changes. Strong and chaotic, her raft pitches against a backdrop of natural disasters. Together they adapt to and tame this new environment, porous to every sensitive fault line.

detail.description:
POROUS MATTER explores the porosity of the body, an open network of relationships between microbes, data and resonances. Many fields of research have become aware of the interconnection of biological systems: our bodies are not closed entities but permeable ones, in constant exchange with their environment. The body is questioned here as an archive of evolving memories, fossil traces and microbiological histories. Bacteria, fungi and cell colonies shape our metabolism and our perception, and remind us that the extinction of species also affects the inhabitants of our own bodies. In this immersive digital walk, the body becomes landscape and host. Screens open windows onto microscopic worlds, making visible what connects us to other forms of life.

title: Li(e)n

detail.description: Three women enter a space shaped by linen, bound by an invisible code: if I hold out my hand, you help me; if I offer you support, I rise. In this fragile architecture, the bodies imprint their breath until one of them breaks the pact. The Tower of Babel then collapses, the fabrics fall and the structure sinks into a chaos of rolls. From this destruction a vortex of struggle is born, where each one tries to climb alone, only to slip inevitably. The body can only rise through collaboration. Through a circular ritual, the artists explore collective work to raise the elements back up like a tree of life. LI(E)N is an unprecedented exploration of matter and solidarity, inviting us to rethink how we inhabit the world, together.

detail.description: A man arrives at a place where his friend Georges has disappeared. From this absent body, carrots have grown, both garden and viscera, promises and remains. Projet Carotte is a hybrid of circus, electronic music and visual art installation that questions the cycles of transformation: grief that becomes compost, compost that becomes life, loss that becomes celebration... Between ritual and investigation, the show celebrates the vital impulse in the face of collapse. How do we go on when everything is changing? In an intimate space, Projet Carotte questions, with humor and tenderness, our relationship to desire, to life and to getting moving. We discover an unpredictable, playful clown who draws us into his obsessive quest for a carrot, inviting us to savor the pleasure of being alive.

title: Don Baltha
summary: At the age of three, he was dressed up for the first time as Balthazar... He would have preferred to be the cow, but his skin and his unruly hair had assigned him the role of the black...

detail.description: At the age of three, he was dressed up for the first time as Balthazar... He would have preferred to be the cow, but his skin and his unruly hair had assigned him the role of the black wise man of the biblical tales. As if in a loop, every year, being the only Black child in a Catholic school in Ecuador, he had to play this character again in the living nativity scene organized at Christmas. Over time, this condition became a powerful strength that motivated him to confront inequality and celebrate diversity. Don Baltha is an Afro-surrealist circus solo blending juggling, dance and acrobatics in an autobiographical story with provocative humor, to question, transform and transcend the absurdity found in every form of dehumanization and stigmatization.

title: BLACK OUT ou comment laisser passer la lumière
summary: BLACK OUT is an invitation to board the same boat: the absolutely madcap one of characters trying to knock Chaos out. That Chaos that keeps shaking everything, that breaks destinies that...

detail.description: BLACK OUT is an invitation to board the same boat: the absolutely madcap one of characters trying to knock Chaos out. That Chaos that keeps shaking everything, that breaks destinies that never asked for anything, in short, that insists on putting a spoke in the wheel of our lives... To face it, the audience is invited into a magic circle drawn right in the city: a ceremony is about to take place. Here, we make room for what we usually bury, we invent ways to give ourselves courage. We thumb our noses at despair before running away like kids. We play with our half-empty glasses to try to laugh at the worst, tenderly. We build a poetic shelter that lets us share what cannot be said head-on: those stories each of us carries in our wake, in our silences and our metaphors.

detail.description: When the image frees itself from the body, what remains of the real? HELDA is a choreographic creation blending dance, music and video projection, exploring the relationship between the body and its double. Through work on shadow, light and visual illusions, the spectator's bearings shift. The body becomes in turn matter, silhouette and apparition, in constant dialogue with the projected image. The show plays with perception and the limits of the visible, creating a shifting universe where the real grows blurred. A nocturnal form designed for public space, where the mapping and video adapt to each place to reveal a new reading of it.

detail.description: Dare to look at yourself face to face, smile at yourself, hold out your hand, let the reflection be without judgment. Dare to see yourself as you have never seen yourself. Are you capable of it? They roam, pushing their strange carts. Don't be afraid, come closer: when you are alone in front of the mirror, invisible truths or your deepest wishes will appear. Magic happens when things stop being what they are. Miroir, Suis-je ? is a poetic street intervention created by Stéphanie Coppé. Through a play of mirrors, the spectator sees their face transformed while a soundtrack slips into their ears, a reflection of the state of the world around us. And for those who want to take the experience further, when the carts stop, the spectator is invited to listen, on headphones, to contemporary poetry texts about identity.

So, with a basket filled with a magnifying glass and plant elements, two singer-musicians (double bass and cello) and a narrator welcome you to this offering that feels like a picnic on the grass. Many gatherings and encounters around the Plant world took place from July 2025 to July 2026 at the Maison de Quartier des Aubépins in Chalon-sur-Saône. A gentle immersion into the world of lullabies, BERCER LE TEMPS invites you on a journey aboard a rocking chair. Set down in the middle of the city, in a park, a square or a pedestrian street corner, this participatory installation welcomes you into a suspended space-time that contrasts with urban hustle. Feet in the grass, to the rhythm of the rocking, lend an ear to its murmurs and let yourself be carried away by the echoes of childhood through songs from here and elsewhere, with more than 2,700 lullabies in 106 languages. The mobile recording studio set up in an old Westfalia opens its door to those who wish to share a singing memory and leave a trace in turn. The intimate, collective and unifying heritage of the oral tradition of lullabies is then reawakened.

title: La Boite de Pandore
summary: Alone on stage, she builds her little theater. She borrows the little girl of her childhood, to try to make her say a little. A universe between bedroom and clearing, a wild-boar...

detail.description:
Alone on stage, she builds her little theater. She borrows the little girl of her childhood, to try to make her say a little. A universe between bedroom and clearing, a wild-boar predator mask. It speaks of a silence of 14 years. Of everything that was never supposed to be said. It also speaks of the joy of managing to live in the present.
Through the aerial rope, knife throwing, a child-clown and an electric guitar, she tells her story in fragments: adolescence punctuated by joys and black holes caused by sexual violence, the trial, adulthood. She uses circus to “just” manage to say it.
Marion Coulomb takes on a difficult, serious and sensitive subject without ever hurting, where circus remains the central act. The gamble pays off, with Pépita Car directing. Poignant!
“A tribute to circus. A fight for lightness” - La Terrasse
Warning: this show may be upsetting.

title: Smooth As Fiasco
summary: On this muddy day, deep in a swamp, a group of individuals gathers to celebrate. Festive and outlandish ceremonies, funny and pathetic, take place. All in the same mire, the different...

detail.description: On this muddy day, deep in a swamp, a group of individuals gathers to celebrate. Festive and outlandish ceremonies, funny and pathetic, take place. All in the same mire, the different relationships appear and moods surface. Some want to express themselves at all costs while others get bogged down in their own thoughts. Often overwhelmed by events, the characters, despite themselves, cultivate a chaotic and burlesque tableau. Each is guided by their fevers, and letting them out seems the only remedy to avoid sinking collectively into this thick, sticky mud. They all share the same goal: to climb out of the soft earth in which they are drowning. Celebrate or sink, their motto for not getting stuck... forever.

detail.description: A choreographic creation for seven performers, blending contemporary dance and Argentine tango. Dancers, a circus artist and a singer move in a space with no fixed landmarks or unity of time. Through the meeting of different aesthetics, Viens M'embrasser scrutinizes the individual, observes their needs and encounters, and pulses to the rhythm of vital impulses: to love, to belong, to connect, to embrace, to kiss. Against a backdrop of retro music, electro, tango and live singing, bodies commit, norms waver, clichés explode. Feminine and masculine intermingle. No sequined dresses, but tuxedos and scarlet lipstick for everyone, in this piece that blurs the boundaries of gender. Viens M'embrasser is an emotional show to be received with the skin: like a shiver running through you, a reassuring embrace, a surprising blow.

Open your eyes, miss the step and discover: moments of suspension and strolls, tales of clumsiness, pleas in praise of dyspraxia, situations to try more and fail worse. Aïe Boum Zut - malhabile questions, through absurdity, the relationship we have with failure, the unexpected, and the pride of knowing how to use something without spilling it.

detail.description: Two humans who, against all odds, become an unlikely duo, simply because they learned to throw objects in the air, thereby avoiding throwing their own lives up in the air. Fratello features two brothers in life, talented acrobatic bases, who have shared a common passion for circus since their earliest years. A true exploration of brotherhood, this show asks how two bases can create a unique language without the support of a flyer. This bond, woven from trust and complicity, unfolds through varied circus techniques such as juggling, unicycle and floor acrobatics. All of it serves to offer a moment of entertainment and poetry, while highlighting the strength of the brotherly bond and the ability to communicate without words.

title: Adulte
summary: I grow up and I wait to feel it, that moment when the existential crises calm down, the constant self-questioning, the doubts, the fears... that moment of solidity, that reasonable...

detail.description: I grow up and I wait to feel it, that moment when the existential crises calm down, the constant self-questioning, the doubts, the fears... that moment of solidity, that reasonable person we are supposed to become when we become adults. I grow up and I wait, but it doesn't come. So I wonder, is that normal? Do I have a problem? Am I just useless and incapable of getting there? Adulte is about that little voice that is always there to tell us that, whatever we do, we will never measure up. Adulte is also a chance to blend my gaze with that of other people and to look at how we all manage with this evolution we are told is “natural” but that is not natural at all. Some will surely say it is a kind of free therapy. Come to think of it, that's not entirely wrong!

detail.description: On the street corner, two slightly punk buddies, Ded and Steven. One tinkers with music on cassettes, the other makes special effects out of planks and wood screws. They hope to reach for the stars by performing their homemade rock opera in praise of Fabrice Guy. This man, who became Olympic champion in Nordic combined at Albertville in 1992, can now be run into every day. They retrace the epic of their hero in a simple, raw, spectacular way, a bit like themselves... Fabrice Guy is a local figure. Around here, everybody knows him. There are those who were at the side of the track the day of his winning race, those who gave a class presentation about him in fifth grade, those who bumped into him by chance. He is a bit like a neighbor crowned with the glow of an Olympic title. Behind the hero, there is always a story that touches...

detail.description:
At a flea market, Paul decides to part with his childhood toys, and a dialogue begins with his teddy bear. Through this encounter, he tenderly dives back into his memories and goes through the defining moments of his childhood. Inspired by a personal story, the show delicately addresses the themes of childhood wounds, bullying and sexual violence. It questions the silences imposed, particularly on boys, who are often encouraged to hide their emotions and fragilities. It also stages traumatic amnesia: the disorders, doubts, vertigo and dissociative mechanisms that come with these imposed silences. Théodore, ou le silence des hommes invites reflection, listening and speaking out, and can lead to a time for discussion.
Warning: this show may be upsetting.

title: Brusco
summary: A clown solo by Andrea Menozzi that asks us about the fragility of the line between madness and crazy social norms. Boxed in, crushed, constrained by what is expected of us, by what is...

detail.description: A clown solo by Andrea Menozzi that asks us about the fragility of the line between madness and crazy social norms. Boxed in, crushed, constrained by what is expected of us, by what is acceptable, reasonable, reassuring, we all risk losing ourselves, or losing others and the world. The individual is increasingly isolated, standardized, conditioned, so abstraction can become a choice of great wisdom. Each of us has met, on a street corner or leaning at a bar counter, someone outside the frame who, with an incomprehensible sentence, enlightened us with a great truth or pointed out the poetry of a moment. Brusco is the character who disturbs and charms us, the one who shakes us up when we dig in on our certainties. He opens for us a breach into a universe where snow falls in summer thanks to a small flame.

summary: It is the story of a woman, one who has an abortion. It is the story of that gray zone: being happy to have the right to it but sad to use it. Like a window she opens onto her intimacy...

detail.description:
It is the story of a woman, one who has an abortion. It is the story of that gray zone: being happy to have the right to it but sad to use it. Like a window she opens onto her intimacy, Madame Red proudly displays her interior for all to see: a warm, comfortable, red interior. The lair of the beginning and the end of this story: a living room with a womb-like air. Madame Red comes home from a trip, and in her heart-shaped suitcase are all the people she met there. The characters follow one another like the plurality of voices swirling in the head of someone who hesitates. And in her head and around it, music resounds and punctuates her journey. It talks about abortion; it talks about it to laugh about it, to exorcise it and to give voice to what we are used to whispering: making an “event” of this “non-event.” A SHOW WHERE THE COFFEE GETS PUKED UP!
Warning: this show may be upsetting.

detail.description: What if reality surpassed fiction? INVERTÉBRÉS is the story of Clara, a biohacker who, driven by a degenerative disease, modifies her DNA. By pushing the frontiers of science, she triggers a mutation in her body. Gravity no longer seems to act on her, Clara takes flight but, in the same movement, escapes her human nature. The piece distorts your perceptions to explore the prospects of the biotechnological revolution propelling humanity toward unknown horizons. An invitation to bioethical reflection answering the call of geneticist biologists. “I have just jumped into a void no human being has explored before me. I designed a guide RNA specific to my failing cells. The serum now flows in my veins and, like a silent messenger, it seeks its target. I watch for every shiver like an omen. I am on the lookout the way you wait for a storm...” Clara

summary: Le Strip de Chantal is a cry of Love. How do we get out of the clichés that lock us in and give us complexes? Taking striptease somewhere other than the boxes where it is usually...

detail.description:
Le Strip de Chantal is a cry of Love. How do we get out of the clichés that lock us in and give us complexes? Taking striptease somewhere other than the boxes where it is usually placed. The work is really about a tease, a slow unveiling. This show is a way of desexualizing the human body, of finding a freedom, a breath that is often held back by old ancestral codes. A space around modesty, around accepting ourselves with our qualities and our flaws. Imagine the character Carmen Cru putting on a show at the Moulin Rouge in Paris, or Coluche playing James Bond. Le Strip de Chantal is a look at the situation of today's lower social classes. Life is becoming so expensive that we will all have to do as Chantal and Jean-Benoît do: organize inte-grail wellness sessions for the well-being of humanity.

This creation explores ecological fractures as the reflection of our break with the living world. The ground becomes an anchor point for the dancers and a poetic prism: the foundation of all fertility, the place where death is transformed to bring life back. In a society where organic soils are disappearing in favor of inert surfaces, this bond is unraveling. Through intense dances, rooted but fragile, and through words, Hors Sol seeks to make this world beneath visible, and to revive, honor and defend this essential bond. A sensitive attempt at reconciliation.

detail.description: A team of scientists studies a strange and potentially dangerous living matter: the Other Thing. To understand it, these eight mute and endearing characters carry out very methodical and secure research, but following an unprecedented contact between the Other Thing and one of them, they are thrown into turmoil, because for the first time the Other Thing blooms. Between collective decisions and personal initiatives, respect for protocol and phases of panic, the team tries, as best it can, to manage this situation that upends and confronts them, in a great derailment that changes their view of the Other Thing and of their own research. This collective transition toward freedom from protocol and a plunge into the unknown unfolds entirely in images and music in a kind of living cartoon, against a backdrop of musical comedy and scientific experiments.

summary: Beste Cantate is a celebration of folklore and of the power of costumed bodies that meet and transform. Drawing on the Dunkirk carnival and queer imagination, eight dancers explore...

detail.description: Beste Cantate is a celebration of folklore and of the power of costumed bodies that meet and transform. Drawing on the Dunkirk carnival and queer imagination, eight dancers explore the subversive role of popular celebration and ask: how do we imagine a new carnival, both festive and committed? How do we redraw its contours and “make carnival” today? For if carnival touches the greatest number in human, social, spiritual and artistic ways, and offers a precious space of freedom and irreverence, it also has its dark sides. In response to these racist and sexist excesses, Beste Cantate sweeps us into a physical, collective jubilation, reinvents the farandoles, the circles, the band, the rigodons (rowdy dances) of carnival and reclaims the positive force of this historical and cultural heritage.

If injustice is so glaring and so unbearable to us, are we in the right place? Should we put our bodies on the line, even a little more? title: Chiche?!
summary: Four enigmatic, colorful characters appear in the soundscape. Little by little, they poeticize certain ordinary objects found in the environment, adding as if by magic appendages...

detail.description: Four enigmatic, colorful characters appear in the soundscape. Little by little, they poeticize certain ordinary objects found in the environment, adding as if by magic appendages, transformable and inflatable elements... The air then begins to vibrate with unheard-of resonances and harmonies. All with poetry, humor, and... without electricity! Dare you?! Chiche?! is a sound, poetic and ecological show that bets on freeing itself from everything digital and even from electricity, in a roaming form imagined on site. “Chiche” as in frugal, thrifty, modest; and “chiche?” as in a dare, an adventure, an unknown path. Chiche?! is for audiences of all generations, including very young ears, and brings them together, without barrier of language or culture, in the same sensitive and attentive listening.

summary: Biographies is a piece for a juggler and a rapper, in which the audience is invited into the juggler's intimacy and can hear her thoughts. She juggles to the rhythm of her reflections...

detail.description:
Biographies is a piece for a juggler and a rapper, in which the audience is invited into the juggler's intimacy and can hear her thoughts. She juggles to the rhythm of her reflections, which are declaimed for the audience by a rapper. She follows the flow of her thoughts, sometimes precise, sometimes abstract. The juggling echoes them, the throws are timed word by word, and the figures connect to the words sometimes illustratively and sometimes more abstractly. A special relationship links the juggler and the rapper. He is her spokesperson, he knows her thoughts by heart. And he will remember them in 10 years, in 30 years, because he never forgets a rhyme. The text will remain unchanged in his head, unlike the show itself, which will gradually age along with its performers.

detail.description: Faced with the first power cuts at the end of 2028, Ana, then a teenager, refuses to be a passive victim of change. It is the signal of a radical and joyful commitment: no question of enduring, but of reinventing, even if it means giving up 4K streaming. She has developed a bike that generates electricity. A concrete resilience device that keeps music, dance and connection circulating... while also making up for the laziness of going to the gym. Today, July 23, 2046, Ana is going to have you test the energy of change. Welcome to this new reality! ENFIN is a political fiction and a celebration where the story of collapse tips into creative momentum. It is the story of what we accomplished collectively between 2026 and 2046.

detail.description: When Georges dies, his four friends promise each other to look for the ideal tribute. They have been scouring the roads for a year, and still haven't found it. To top it all off, their little truck breaks down and there they are, stuck on the side of the road. What if it were a sign? On the turn of a guitar chord, a door opens onto an afterlife full of humor and tenderness, where the dead may not have said their last word... With Goodbye Georges, the company l'Engrenage tackles the question of grief by blending theater, music and cabaret. In this burlesque and supernatural street show, four characters take the audience along on their impossible quest for the perfect farewell, poetically tracing a possible path between the living and the dead.

summary: One day, the outstretched hand of a beggar stops the tightrope walker Arthur Sidoroff. He lingers, talks with him over a few coffees. From this encounter a story is born. Two meters off...

detail.description: One day, the outstretched hand of a beggar stops the tightrope walker Arthur Sidoroff. He lingers, talks with him over a few coffees. From this encounter a story is born. Two meters off the ground, accompanied by the musician Thomas Caillou, he tells on his wire these fragile and unstable lives. In a two-sided setup conducive to encounter, Robert n'a pas de paillettes offers a suspended journey, where the wire becomes choreographic and sensitive material. Imbalances and catches resonate with our humanity. The show becomes a shared, intimate space where invisible bonds are woven. Arthur Sidoroff asserts a raw, sincere presence, standing on the wire without filters, without artifice.

title: FAUDRAIT PAS RESTER PLANTÉS LÀ
summary: This show is a slice of life, a moment to share. A space to dare to be fragile. To lose your footing, lose your sense of direction and finally let go and savor the absurdity. They are...

detail.description: This show is a slice of life, a moment to share. A space to dare to be fragile. To lose your footing, lose your sense of direction and finally let go and savor the absurdity. They are here. Her. Him. An empty space. A bike. And everything that might happen, at any moment. They go in circles, they face each other, they dance, fall and roll in the dust. Bodies fly, pile up, stumble. They clash and harmonize. The voices speak, shout and laugh. It talks about time passing too fast, about things to do, too many, about guilt, about a galloping horse, about kicking up dust, about leaving yourself alone. We shouldn't just stand there! And why not... They arrived, there was nothing. They left and something had changed. Behind them, the reminiscences of their transformation. Ephemeral traces, swept away by the next gust of wind.

summary: “Okay, it's late, I'm going home. I'd better take off before that guy notices me... Everyone left, though: I'm going home alone... and on foot... Okay... I'm going.” Specializing in...

detail.description: “Okay, it's late, I'm going home. I'd better take off before that guy notices me... Everyone left, though: I'm going home alone... and on foot... Okay... I'm going.” Specializing in hybrid forms blending cinema, performance and live theater, our company offers a singular form here. Two women, an actress and a technician, take the reins of a film shoot that hems them in and pigeonholes them. The audience then accompanies them in their decision to be done with the cinematic codes of fear, and also to propose new stories, alternative ways of being together outside the dominant system of FEAR. Alternating personal narrative, shooting and live editing with the spectators, projection on walls and laughter, the show offers different space-times that open new horizons each time.

detail.description: Loosely adapted from the comic book The Origin of the World by Liv Strömquist, published by Rackham, Le Fruit de la Connaissance tackles, with humor and impertinence, the story of a discovery. That of the “vluve” (the vulva), its history, its anatomy, but also the symbols, myths and medical theories associated with it over the centuries, and its disastrous appropriation by men. From Antiquity to the Middle Ages by way of the dreadful nineteenth century, the actresses take us on the trail of the construction of our imagination of the sex historically and socially assigned to the female gender.

detail.description: A show blending theater, storytelling, objects and music, this creation follows the quiet life of Marie-Jeanne and the regulars of the bar La Consolatrice, upended by the arrival of the Marshal-President, a dictator who subverts democracy to seize power. Backed by large multinationals, he exploits mineral resources, destroys villages and pushes inhabitants into exile. Through this story, Compagnie Hardie denounces political excesses, the effects of globalization and their human and social consequences. True to its universe, the company blends storytelling, poetry and satire in a free and inventive writing style, oscillating between humor, social criticism and philosophical reflection. Behind an apparent simplicity, the show questions deep, existential issues.

summary: Sensible is a dive into the murky and clear waters of what makes up our images of man. Through this popular show, we invite the audience to confront their own sensitivities and question...

detail.description: Sensible is a dive into the murky and clear waters of what makes up our images of man. Through this popular show, we invite the audience to confront their own sensitivities and question masculinities. The question is not what a man is, but rather what we want him to be. So we offer an exploration of man with a small “m,” of the masculine absurdity of our time and of our own constructions. With self-mockery, Sensible leaves room for reflection, tenderness and self-acceptance. It aims to be the gentle key to open a dialogue around this theme that has seemed to us hidden behind a closed door for a long time. Sensible is an immersion in exploring the masculinities around which we built ourselves, in what we are at our most terrible and most beautiful.

Can small countries make the most of their hand? Between music, dance, sidewalk magic and joyful propaganda, Kik soft power lands.

detail.description: In a peripheral neighborhood infested with rats, residents, all night workers, gather after one of their children has been bitten. The image of this child, a rat hanging from his bloody hand, floats in every mind. What to do? A nursing assistant, a cleaner, a parking attendant, a night-owl partygoer and a rat specialist chaotically try to find a solution. But from the first question, how to eradicate the rats that have invaded us, comes a collective reflection on the responsibility of those in power, their own invisibility in the eyes of those who decide, and on the rats themselves: who are really the pests of whom? From a neighborhood meeting to a stroll of residents ready to make themselves visible, Nuisibles offers to take the audience into an act of collective power.

detail.description: “C'est carré” (“it's square”), this expression has been used since 2010 to mean that everything is settled properly. For this cube-headed character, not everything is square: the gestures are curved, the movements round off the lines as if to counter the rigidity of his world. Mischievous geometric contradictions will lead him to walk on his head! He bends, springs, slides, loses his balance and traces circles in squares to share the drawing of his emotions. It is around a 4x4 meter square floor that this atypical being invites you to dive into an intimate, funny and acrobatic universe. C'EST CARRÉ is a visual, poetic and wordless journey, where circus becomes language and the body a ground for emancipation.

summary: One day, Camille lied to her friends Laurine and Marguerite. The day the truth came out, they wanted to understand: why do we lie? Based on interviews, the three actresses carry out...

detail.description:
One day, Camille lied to her friends Laurine and Marguerite. The day the truth came out, they wanted to understand: why do we lie? Based on interviews, the three actresses carry out an anatomy of lying, which leads us down the (false) trails of human truth. What truth hides behind our lies? What is this terror of being only ourselves that pushes us to fabricate a myth of ourselves?
À la limite de la crédibilité is a kaleidoscopic story inspired by a series of testimonies. Three actresses take hold of these stories before an audience attending a ceremony of self-revelation. Perhaps they will recognize themselves...
“We lie to hide. To hide but to be found. For hiding is a pleasure but not being found is a catastrophe.” Donald Winnicott

detail.description: La Société des Belles Personnes invites the audience into the heart of a vibrant, almost euphoric party, where collective intensity sweeps bodies away, all the way through our fragilities and flaws. This creation questions our relationship to dance and to partying today. Why do we dance less? Which social frameworks keep us from being fully ourselves? By amplifying traits and reality, the spectator undergoes a real transformation over the course of an evening. Carried by a company of young artists, La Société des Belles Personnes claims an embodied and deeply human dance. Cradled by the live music of PËNDÄMØNIUM, this creation is an invitation to come together, across classes, genders and origins, to celebrate the beauty of being together. Here, dance becomes a social and liberating act, a call to let go of the codes and join the party.

summary: A street acrobatic duo where men are like birds on a branch. A passerby happens upon a café table under a pergola. Dans l'Ombre des Oiseaux lacks nothing to be an idyllic place. Except...

detail.description: A street acrobatic duo where men are like birds on a branch. A passerby happens upon a café table under a pergola. Dans l'Ombre des Oiseaux lacks nothing to be an idyllic place. Except perhaps a glass of water. But as in all paradise stories, there is an Other. Nothing serious, but everything we thought we had for ourselves has to be shared. And there, with no shade to hide in, everything shows, from physical differences to character traits. You think a parasol would be enough? Plant one in paradise and everything starts to sway up to 7 meters high. Reality capsizes and the two men aboard cling to each other to stay upright.

detail.description:
Research lab showing: 1h50 walk
Kalinka explored the body, the voice and matter before writing. Anaïs explored spaces and languages before writing. Kalinka discovered street theater almost by chance. Anaïs discovered theatrical writing almost by chance. Both know the language of cinema and the stage. From the moment they met, their writings resonated with each other. They exchange their texts, recognizing a shared sensibility. What links them appears: a common interest in family ties, in the group, in what binds individuals. Nourished by experience and by the news about changing conditions of detention, the subject of their research imposes itself: detention. During the weeks of residency, they will discover the realities of families, loved ones, people facing waiting, absence, uncertainty. The showing of their research lab will consist of presenting the striking images collected and connecting them to one another.

title: Viriles
summary: Five men. Five trajectories shaped by an inherited virility, almost inscribed in the flesh. On stage, they confront others, themselves, trying to embody an ideal that exceeds them. Then a...

detail.description:
Five men. Five trajectories shaped by an inherited virility, almost inscribed in the flesh. On stage, they confront others, themselves, trying to embody an ideal that exceeds them. Then a crack. Under the tension, long-contained emotions surface, intimacy and sensitivity. They walk through their own construction as a ground to be deconstructed, letting fragility, ambivalence and nuance emerge. Between control and surrender, they seek a balance, a more intimate truth. Carried by five female performers, the piece shifts gazes and unsettles bearings. Gender boundaries blur, identities circulate. A space opens where each person can redefine their body and the way they inhabit it.
Warning: this show may be upsetting.

detail.description: Olivier is a cook. He is also a gardener. And a beekeeper. But above all, Olivier is obsessed with time. A mysterious individual asked him to bring a group of people to Chalon for an unknown mission that will last 8,760 hours, with a break of 8,758 hours. How? You will find out. Why? He has no idea. But he is convinced, he feels it, it is worth it. So he invites you to join him in the adventure. Walking at his side, listening to him tell us about his practice of cooking, beekeeping and the landscape, Olivier draws us into an enigmatic, intimate and temporal quest. But where does it lead us? Suspense! With this fable to live together, Olivier has us practice, hear and taste a landscape by offering an unprecedented experience of time, very different from that of our calendars. A science-fiction experience that is pastoral, gustatory, in a living landscape.

title: Par-delà l'horizon

detail.description: Today, I sculpt space and time, exploring the relativity of risk: what seems perilous becomes a ground for fine perception and dialogue with the void. Written in 360°, the piece seeks to reveal the thickness of gravity while unfolding a singular poetry. An acrobat moves on a seven-meter wind turbine, a kind of reinvented wheel of death. She oscillates between the aerial and the earthly, creating dramatic tension. The live music shifts between three universes: the atmospheric sounds of Blade Runner, a piano in the vein of Ryuichi Sakamoto's sounds, and deeply expressive telluric percussion. Par-delà l'horizon is a living piece cultivating the pure pleasure of movement and sound.

detail.description: Batman is a shaman. Between joyful science, poetic texts and electronic music, the company Mycélium proposes exchanging signals with bats through an ultrasound detector that lets you sing and make music with them during an initiatory vigil, a real experience of contact with other species, an invitation to become aware of the beauty of other ways of existing. The team has a bat-box (a micro receiver) that turns the ultrasounds emitted by bats into sounds audible to the human ear, and a system that turns speech, songs and music into ultrasounds for bats. A receiver, a transmitter, frequencies on both sides: dialogue can begin, the symphony can start...

detail.description: Inside a caravan grows a forest sheltering two sisters and their hut. They tell the story of their people facing rising waters, one drawing in the sand, the other translating these drawings aloud. This new creation, the second episode of On boira toute l'eau du ciel, focuses this time on the survival and adaptation of the community. By gently approaching environmental issues through a timeless tale and placing the act of invention as a necessity, it restores a little hope in our worrying global political context. Moving drawings in the sand to tell the story, a narrator carrying the voice of a people, a spatialized sound creation: Comment j'ai appris à pêcher is a striking immersive experience from which the audience does not leave quite the same.

detail.description: Camera Obscura is a setup that offers the audience the unique experience of a film screening without electricity. Spectators settle inside the camera obscura and watch the projection of a film made in real time outside. The images are projected through an optical system of lenses and mirrors. The sounds and music are produced and performed live on a set of acoustic and mechanical instruments. The film shown is Souvenirs du futur. It is a collection of fragments, vague or anecdotal evocations of possible futures. Speculative stories that break free from science-fiction themes and offer a vision that is neither utopian nor apocalyptic of a plural, banal and strange future.

detail.description: How important is a frame to a work? What happens if you remove it? Or conversely: what happens if you only look at the frame? Frames explores this relationship between frame and work, placing the physical art of Not Standing in outdoor visual frames. Alexander Vantournhout and his three partners create constantly evolving body sculptures within the viewing frames. Bodies intertwine, hang and climb on the frames, walk upside down and defy gravity as well as your imagination. Each movement is a permanent search for balance, focused on cooperation and body control. Frames invites you to explore choreographic installations that challenge artistic and visual perspectives, turning them into physical poetry within public space.

Birds that make us cohabit with the wild everywhere and all the time. It is an immersive poetic science fiction that creates plays of mirrors between them and us. detail.description: Et toi, qu'est-ce que tu portes ? is a crossing of space without touching the ground. In the distance, a duo forms, one becomes the other's territory, their trajectory stretches toward the audience. Close to it, an actress carries a text that crosses the distance and links their bodies to the space, the environment and the audience, gently questioning what we are, through the lift. At the heart of this journey, the relationship, the bond with the other. After three years of research around the question “And you, what are you carrying?”, the company returns to public space with this show in order to lay down, in its own way, the answers of the people met along the research. Laëtitia Andrieu's texts are the link between the sensitive bodies and the places crossed.

Underground is a piece about the invisible in which a dancer's body and the words that accompany it give access to an impenetrable world: that underground, so close and yet forever unknown. The other side of the mirror. Plunging into the Underground means placing the body at a border: in the world of the living but also a little elsewhere. And there, at the edge of crossing over, looking for what springs up, what moves, what dances. What keeps us alive, in spite of everything.

detail.description: Andrej, a fresh graduate, fights to land a job; Martina, from a well-off background, dreams of an organic farm but keeps landing lousy jobs; Mani, a brilliant academic, is out of work; Freya, just laid off, craves revenge; and Peter, homeless, has become an expert in street marketing. All of them, without always knowing it, take part in a competition as vile as it is human for their survival. With mischievous detachment, Jonas Hassen Khemiri chooses to tell, through five interwoven stories, the perversity of lacking money and its harmful consequences on an intimate scale. With exemplary dramatic irony, he intertwines the destinies of these figures so close to us. “Almost equal to is a funny and biting contemporary comedy about the world of capitalism, its antiheroes and our schizophrenic relationship to money.”

title: La Recomposition des Mondes

detail.description: Politicians desperately try to get rid of power so they can focus on their community gardens, while chickadees go into politics with Molotov cocktails; a riot police officer in the middle of burnout confides in a team of journalists who try, for better or worse, to understand what is going on. Judging by the many demonstrations blooming everywhere, a (r)evolution is under way. What remains to be seen is where it will lead. Imagine a world where the nature/culture opposition has been abolished and where the dominant way of thinking leans toward animism. This is the kind of situation the author Alessandro Pignocchi depicts in his graphic novels “just to make my friends laugh,” he says, and also “because it feels good to imagine fictions where the changes we would like to see in the world take place.”

detail.description: Am I a good parent? If you are asking yourself this question, it is probably time to take part in our parenting points recovery course. Under the kind, but firm, eye of Carole and Cédric, our two certified experts in intensive educational coaching, you will benefit from practical advice, realistic role-plays and personalized support to (re)become an exemplary parent, one to make the parent-teacher representatives and other cookie-baking experts green with envy. Between absurd lecture and dubious methods, this course humorously pins down the contradictory demands, anxieties and absurdities that surround parenting today. Because parenting is like the pelvic floor: it is a muscle. And when it is slack, you have to retrain it. Permissive, authoritarian, disengaged parents, what kind of parent are you?

detail.description: In this creation carried by Betty Mansion and Médhi Beduin, four friends meet in a space where emotions overflow. Bodies flail, contradict each other, search for each other. Feelings take up too much room, gestures skid, situations run away. Here, everyday neuroses become material for play and transformation. Between absurd impulses and moments of fragility, each one crosses their flaws before rejoining the group. Dance allows itself everything: the beautiful as well as the wobbly, the controlled as well as the overflowing. It brings out what words leave unsaid. An invigorating and sensitive show, shot through with humor, where we laugh, waver and recognize ourselves.

detail.description:
To discover Scélérates you have to take on water, so we will dive in together, in swimsuits or costumes, into the Saint-Rémy pool. Facing rising waters together, creating cross-species alliances and imagining new stories, becoming chimeras. “Scélérate” (rogue wave) denotes an unpredictable wave, a wall of water that strikes ships without warning, that transforms the sea and the world. To turn our view of submersion upside down together: celebrating joyful disappearances and making room for what comes next, with joy and determination. Rather than resisting or denying, it is about going along with the movement. A poetic and collective experience to invent, together, sensitive forms of transformation in the face of crises. And to celebrate our futures. Aquatic show: don't forget your swimsuit.

summary: These are the intertwined stories of several characters around a dam. The story of several trout and a few perch swimming at the bottom of an artificial lake, and of birds that carry us...

detail.description: These are the intertwined stories of several characters around a dam. The story of several trout and a few perch swimming at the bottom of an artificial lake, and of birds that carry us across the ocean and through time. We expect a well-built thriller, when, little by little, we are immersed in the questions and the turmoil of those who tell the story. How do you build a show today, as observers of our own excesses? This is one of the big questions driving this collective, which stretches a taut thread on which the drops of past and future struggles bead, between the beginning and the end of the story; between the solid foundations of a story being told and the dreamlike deconstruction of a collapsing universe. A poetic and musical show where the puppeteers, as necessary shadows, work with precision and fluidity.

So don't hesitate to bring your guys, your buddies, your dads, your grandpas: at one point, we offer to slap them and we really do it, then we hang out laundry full of blood. title: Loup y es tu ?
summary: A committed, tender and funny tale about our collective fears. A new mayor has been elected unanimously. He swore, promised, spat: “No more Big Bad Wolf in our town!” The result? He closed...

detail.description: A committed, tender and funny tale about our collective fears. A new mayor has been elected unanimously. He swore, promised, spat: “No more Big Bad Wolf in our town!” The result? He closed off access to the woods and armed the hunter with a bazooka. Just like that! Everyone feels out of danger and never mind if you have to show your passport to stick your nose outside. The little girl in the red hood starts to grumble: “How do I get to see Grandma without getting nabbed? She has no Wi-Fi, no signal, just her old radio! And besides, who has ever run into this Big Bad Wolf?” In this contemporary fable, Amal takes on monsters manufactured to scare us. A family and political show that invites reflection and action.

company: Rêve de Moi, j’Rêve de Toi (Compagnie)
summary: She is called La Petite (The Little One). And her sister is La Grande (The Big One). La Grande has a secret. And La Petite wants to know. She can't help it. Between the two, the threads of...

detail.description: She is called La Petite (The Little One). And her sister is La Grande (The Big One). La Grande has a secret. And La Petite wants to know. She can't help it. Between the two, the threads of a metamorphosis are woven. Inspired by a traditional story from the North American Blackfoot tribe, Ursa Major plunges into the heart of the forest to question the ambivalent and complex bond uniting sisters, becoming oneself, love and everyone's place in the world. The show blends real and fiction, storytelling arts and music, the creation myth of the Great Bear and intimate words of today. It is a tale from the dawn of time that transcends Manichaeism to open a world inhabited by beauty and horror, love and cruelty. A world that intimately links human and nature, life and death.

title: "C'est Gratos"
summary: A Belgian training show blending humor, slapstick, singing, juggling and flutes. In its long form you will learn the 5 stages of successful training, thanks to unconditional love and...

detail.description: A Belgian training show blending humor, slapstick, singing, juggling and flutes. In its long form you will learn the 5 stages of successful training, thanks to unconditional love and also... Domination! “C'est Gratos” is a fable made of little poems performed by two males, one Alpha and the other rather “Beta.” The relationships of domination or submission often illustrated in animal shows are tackled head-on with subtlety, finesse, plenty of intelligence and enormous humor. Mimicry, parody, role reversal... Who dominates whom? Impossible to untangle, and all the better. One thing is certain: when a crested clown and a Chinese crested dog become such accomplices: laughter, emotion and depth are on the bill. Beware, animal.

detail.description: Léila, l'histoire d'une fuite is a hybrid object that faces vertigo and idiocy through wobbly feats, lyrical performances, generously embodied characters and singular dances. An epic blending dance, theater and idiocy in which we follow the character Léila, a “good-natured young adult who loves adventure.” The story begins one evening when she hears a speech by Bruce Lee on the radio, “Be water my friend,” and it is a revelation for Léila, who then decides to set off on the path of her “liquid base.” Nothing will stop her now. It is a matter of life and death. “Maybe you don't know the day you are starting yet, but it doesn't know you either,” her mother always told her. An enchanted interlude that might catch deep questions without seeming to.

detail.description: Suspended from a facade, two bodies explore the space that links and separates them. The building becomes an axis, AXIS, that orients their movement and their relationship to gravity. Between closeness and distance, their movements shift bearings and fully reveal their fragility. In the verticality of the facade, lines and supports draw the space of a relationship where balance, tension and encounter are continually reinvented. But AXIS is at once human and architectural: it manifests as an abstraction that orients the body in its relationship with the other, with gravity and with urban space. Purely rational and yet exposed to the complexity of all that is human.

VIOLENT pulls out everything hidden under the bed and at the back of our heads since childhood, mixes it with memories of a seaside resort and adds the unsold stock of AliExpress. The dancers metamorphose, nothing is tangible anymore, only bodies remain, now just the allegory of a celebration, bodies swallowed by the party. VOLUME 54, an all-terrain dance show about a party... Or rather the body at a party. A suspended time that takes a sensitive look at those who make it a necessity. The mind losing its footing. The dancing step taking over. The party as an expression of urgency. The party anywhere and above all where you don't expect it.

summary: Stéphane comes from sound and listening, Nicolas from theater; one explores sensation, the other dramaturgy; one gives body to spaces, the other works words in space. From this meeting...

detail.description: Stéphane comes from sound and listening, Nicolas from theater; one explores sensation, the other dramaturgy; one gives body to spaces, the other works words in space. From this meeting comes a shared desire: to cross their languages to create an experience. How do you tell a story without imposing a narrative? How does our environment influence the way we perceive, feel and think? How can words stir the senses and enhance an experience? With reality as the score and words as instruments, Stéphane and Nicolas break down the walls between disciplines and experiment with new forms of narration, on the border between a roaming show and a lived experience. During Chalon dans la rue, they will share their journey, the questions driving their research and the first leads taking shape: a textual, sonic and experiential travel log through which the audience will be invited to follow the traces or clues left by a person, an absent presence. Between sound fiction and investigation, spectators become actors in their own perception, invited to listen to and observe their surroundings to move the story forward.

He will in fact have prepared everything so that it goes well, but of course, on this day of torment, how not to falter? How not to be clumsy? So we will share with them the moments we know from a “classic” ceremony: the reception, the feast, the speech, a last word, a last wish, but in the presence of the future deceased. summary: “It's moving! Did you see? No? Are you sure? I swear this bush wasn't there a minute ago... Did you take my crêpe?” There are two of them. One is ready to explore. The other is mostly...

detail.description: “It's moving! Did you see? No? Are you sure? I swear this bush wasn't there a minute ago... Did you take my crêpe?” There are two of them. One is ready to explore. The other is mostly hungry... They camouflage themselves to hunt and survive. In a world where no one looks like them anymore and where food is plentiful, they quickly learn the rules: beg, steal, seduce, compete, fight, ally, worship. Sapiens Sapiens appears to put under our noses a version of ourselves not so far removed. The project seeks to rehabilitate the senses as our first spaces of connection to the world. Before any thought, sensation is, for us, the personal revelation that we exist. “I feel, therefore I am” thus becomes our parable for joyfully healing ourselves of the terrible Western confusion: “I think, therefore I am”!

The roast chicken has taken up the drums, the sausage is playing a part, a beet (that raps and refuses to be grated) wants to knock the steaks out of order... title: T'as pas vu Léon ?
summary: It is the story of Gustave, a lost man who watched the rivers run dry and the life of the meadows of his childhood disappear. A man who, too attached to things of the past, set off on a...

detail.description: It is the story of Gustave, a lost man who watched the rivers run dry and the life of the meadows of his childhood disappear. A man who, too attached to things of the past, set off on a quest beyond him: the search for Léon, his butterfly friend who vanished 20 years ago. A man who let his madness slip away from him. A man who, no longer recognizing a world disfigured by an invisible poison that destroys everything alive, turned into the architect of his own kingdom. Fleeing a system gone mad, he decided to bring back what was taken from him with the little he has left. To create an absurd universe, filled with lepidoptera, myriapods and mantises, in which he feels at ease. An enchanted and disturbing universe. A universe as ephemeral and fragile as newsprint. A universe where his memories and his fabulations allow him, perhaps, to take back his freedom.

summary: Three slightly lost individuals, “surplus people,” anonymous among the anonymous, emerge from the crowd. Unbeknownst to them, they take part in a life-size social psychology...

detail.description: Three slightly lost individuals, “surplus people,” anonymous among the anonymous, emerge from the crowd. Unbeknownst to them, they take part in a life-size social psychology experiment, in turn guinea pigs, witnesses or instigators. How do we collaborate despite our disagreements? Which techniques can be used to manipulate a crowd? What is public opinion? What divides or unites us at our deepest level? Taking advantage of the large number of people present, they try to bring out collective intelligence, the “wisdom of crowds”... or the dumbing down of the masses. Playing with received ideas, ulterior motives and counter-intuitions, they explore this social animal that is the human being. An animal capable of going far... very far. Too far?

detail.description: Juli! tells us about those little things that make up the universality of existence. With her piano, beautiful as life, she questions herself (and us) about death, love, desire... Poetry in its raw state, where words twisted by dyslexia resonate with real truths. She overdoes it, allows herself everything, and that's what we love. Juli! takes us between original performances and improbable ravings. A contagious energy, between laughter, emotion and shared moments of grace. On stage, anything can happen. It springs up, it veers off, it runs away and drags us where we don't expect. We go from laughter to a tightening silence, a moment that catches you, suspends time and lets the words resonate. And then it takes off again, lively and surprising. A living, dazzling and fragile show unfolds before our eyes. Intense, poetic, sometimes funny, sometimes poignant, but always deeply human.

This summer, in Chalon, they offer to share some of their ravings on public transit. Eco-friendly funeral services, travelers swapping lives for the length of a stop, crooner duos announcing the stops, buses turned into restaurants, express romantic comedies... Some scenes come from the texts of the Brigades, written through the Authors in Tandem program (Artcena - 2023-2024). Others were created specially for the occasion, like these new social housing units installed in buses... Some appointments will be announced. detail.description: Mon Aile is the poetic story of a character who lost a wing... or believes they lost it. Inspired by a real accident, this story becomes a universal metaphor for everyone who may, at some point in their life, have lost a “wing.” Through this metaphor, the show speaks to us about encounters and resilience. Between close-up circus, teapot puppetry, parachute dance and live music, the company Yifan unfolds a universe that touches young and old, where humor and emotion intertwine delicately. Presented at international festivals: South Korea, Turkey, India, invited by the Institut Français. “A creation full of wonder and poetry” - La Dépêche

detail.description: Ladies and gentlemen, you who chose to be here, welcome to the Cabaret d'Azar! Here, we will share the magic of being able to turn lead into feathers with a single glance and take flight under the same sky! Come closer! Azar opens the doors of its universe and raises the curtain on its latest show to reveal its enchantment, half-animal and raw, half-human and goosebump-inducing! Come! Let yourself fall from the clouds, where the impossible is tamed to free dreams, where imperfection is turned into virtuosity, where the ordinary becomes extraordinary! Smile! at this stage beast that is none other than our capacity for wonder! Let the show begin... and never stop!

title: CATHARSIS
summary: Two female musicians arrive for an impeccable concert: bold brilliance, total mastery, displayed elegance. But behind their confidence, the dam breaks. Music steps down from its pedestal...

detail.description: Two female musicians arrive for an impeccable concert: bold brilliance, total mastery, displayed elegance. But behind their confidence, the dam breaks. Music steps down from its pedestal, and everything overflows. Through their clumsy attempts to be “proper,” these two women reveal what we all keep quiet: our excesses. They fall, get back up, explode, catch each other, together. They show us that we can lose control, scream, cry, laugh, and that it feels incredibly good. They refuse to be well-behaved, refuse to be boxes. They rough up norms and polite femininity, preferring power, flaw, solidarity. They love each other badly, they love each other hard, they put up with each other, they carry each other, like us in our battered lives. Musical, clownesque, visceral and jubilant theater, where virtuosity serves excess. Everything becomes possible in a collective liberation.

detail.description: Tópec is a mole shepherd. With planets in his pockets, Tópec shares his fascination with the immensity, the secret movements of the sky and his tribe of precious underground ladies, scattered around the neighborhood! Tópec is a wild electron, a haystack of humankind, thick in the thinnest, a patrophysicist at large in the cosmos. In his world, life is round like an orbit, round like an eye socket, and everything revolves around everything, time, water drops, cherry flies, questions, clouds... Come on, come on, ladies and gentlemen, step up and enter the big top of cosmic drafts. Welcome to the groggy, the sharp and brilliant, the fake slow, the lonely stars, and their shoes full of dirt...! Here, there's only one step to the “there's nothing”! Or two or three, depending on the length of your imagination's legs!

detail.description: Have you ever put your hands in the soil? Because in life, that's what Léa likes to do best. She loves it so much that she made it her job: she is a MARKET GARDENER. Accompanied by Jean-Pierre, her colleague the earthworm, she takes us to explore the farm and its mysteries... So come closer, let yourself be carried away by these germinating stories, let a little song grow in you, and above all don't be afraid of messing up and getting your hands dirty! Les Radis, ça compte pas pour du beurre is a show woven from a true story, a ton of curiosity, a wheelbarrow of wonder, a shovelful of musicality, an ounce of love of storytelling and a pinch of nonsense!

detail.description: An old friend of Hippocrates, Doctor Vitale travels the world to take part in its regeneration and reinvent public service. Accompanied by her intern, she sets up at a market, a street corner or a patch of fresh grass, turns the encounter into a consultation, the audience into a patient list, a jumble of objects into instruments, and knits an unprecedented therapeutic performance where everything is cared for. In a few minutes, she dispenses diagnoses, prescriptions, orders. From immune ecstasy to emotional unmolding, by way of the beauty of the aorta and the rest implant, she takes audiences along with aplomb and method, a doctor is very serious. Doctolibre sets up for 3 hours straight: people are seen immediately. In case of a crowd, they sign up for a 15-minute slot and can wait in an improvised waiting area.
